candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — advance directives and health care proxy
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish a durable power of attorney for health care from financial power of attorney and DNR orders: it names a health care agent to act when the person cannot make or communicate health care decisions, within the document and applicable state rules.

options.A: It authorizes an agent to manage only finances and property when the person cannot make decisions.
options.B: It names a health care proxy or agent to make health care decisions if the person cannot make or communicate those decisions, subject to the document and applicable state rules.
options.C: It functions as a do-not-resuscitate order and applies only to resuscitation decisions during cardiopulmonary arrest.
options.D: It transfers all health care decision-making authority to the agent immediately after signing, even while the person remains able to make and communicate decisions.

candidate.rationale: National Institute on Aging guidance describes a durable power of attorney for health care as an advance-directive document that names a health care proxy, representative, surrogate, or agent who can make health care decisions if the person is unable to make or communicate those decisions. The scope and formal requirements can vary by state and by the document. Therefore B is correct. A describes financial/property authority rather than the health care proxy role, C confuses the document with a DNR order, and D incorrectly displaces the decisions of a person who remains able to make and communicate health care choices.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A durable power of attorney for health care names a proxy/agent to make health care decisions when the person cannot make or communicate those decisions; document scope and state rules govern details.
